reason: I'd maybe play with the demo-money version for fun, but I'm not lining up to hand real money and my brokerage access to a brand-new app whose broker partner isn't even named yet. I already ask Claude and then place the trades myself, and that keeps me in control for free.
objection: Is my data and my money safe with a new app? I don't know who the licensed broker is, who holds my account, or what happens to my info if this startup folds, and on top of that I'd be paying a monthly fee on a portfolio under $20k.
would_change_my_mind: Naming a big, known broker that actually holds the money (SIPC-insured, my account in my name) plus a few months of the demo showing it beats what I already do, at a price under about $5 a month.
